title: Harmonic Floor Sums in O(√n)
difficulty: Medium
order: 5
tags: complexity, square root decomposition, math, harmonic series
time_limit: 1
---
## Statement
For a positive integer `n`, compute

- `S(n) = ⌊n/1⌋ + ⌊n/2⌋ + … + ⌊n/n⌋`. This is also the total number of divisors of 1, 2, …, n. Can you see why?
- `D(n)` = the number of **distinct** values among `⌊n/i⌋` for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.

```cpp
std::pair<long long, long long> floor_sum(long long n);   // {S(n), D(n)}
```

n goes up to 10¹², so a loop over all `i` (10¹² steps) is hopeless.

**Key fact:** `⌊n/i⌋` takes only O(√n) distinct values, and every value covers a contiguous **block** of `i`. For a block starting at `i`, the value is `q = ⌊n/i⌋`, and the block ends at `j = ⌊n/q⌋`.

**Input:** `t` (t ≤ 20), then `t` values of `n`. Print `S D` for each.

## Starter
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

pair<long long, long long> floor_sum(long long n) {
    long long s = 0;
    set<long long> seen;
    for (long long i = 1; i <= n; ++i) { s += n / i; seen.insert(n / i); }
    return {s, (long long)seen.size()};
}
```

## Driver
```cpp
int main() {
    int t; cin >> t;
    while (t--) {
        long long n; cin >> n;
        auto [s, d] = floor_sum(n);
        cout << s << ' ' << d << '\n';
    }
}
```

## Hints
- Print `n / i` for n = 20 and every `i`. The same values repeat in runs.
- For a run starting at `i` with value `q = n / i`, the run ends at `n / q`.
- Count the runs: each run is exactly one distinct value.

## Solution
**Why O(√n) distinct values.**

- For `i ≤ √n` there are at most √n different `i`, so at most √n values.
- For `i > √n`, the value `n/i < √n`, so again at most √n possibilities.

Together that's at most 2√n values.

**Block boundaries.** If `q = ⌊n/i⌋`, the largest `j` with `⌊n/j⌋ = q` is `j = ⌊n/q⌋`. Add `q · (j − i + 1)` to the sum and jump to `j + 1`. Each block is one distinct value, so counting the blocks gives `D(n)`.

**Why S(n) counts divisors.** `⌊n/i⌋` counts the multiples of `i` up to `n`. Summing over `i` counts every (divisor, multiple) pair once.

For n = 10¹² that's about 2·10⁶ blocks per query, and S(10¹²) ≈ 2.8·10¹³ fits in `long long`.

Complexity: O(√n) per query.

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

pair<long long, long long> floor_sum(long long n) {
    long long s = 0, blocks = 0;
    for (long long i = 1; i <= n; ) {
        long long q = n / i;          // the value for this whole block
        long long j = n / q;          // the last i with n / i == q
        s += q * (j - i + 1);
        ++blocks;
        i = j + 1;
    }
    return {s, blocks};
}
```
